scene.title: From a Jupyter prototype to a production ticket classifier
scene.sceneHtml:
TicketFlow: Day 1

Your first task at Loomline: take the prototype ticket classifier from a Jupyter notebook to a production Python service. The prototype uses the Messages API to categorize support tickets as billing, technical, or feature_request. Your job: make it reliable, cost-tracked, and ready for real traffic.

takeaways: Request shape: model, max_tokens, system, messages. Response shape: content blocks, stop_reason and usage (input/output tokens).
System prompt holds behavior, tone and output schema; the user message carries this turn's task. Don't scatter rules across both.
Log message.usage.input_tokens and output_tokens for cost tracking: you pay for both, and token tracking is essential for cost management.
Model choice: Haiku for simple, latency/cost-tight tasks; Sonnet for most workloads; Opus for complex reasoning and rare edge cases.
